The Robbery Leaderboard

Every UFC decision, ranked by how strongly the statistics disagree with the result

The Robbery Score is 1 − P(declared winner wins | fight stats). A high score means the round-by-round statistics strongly favoured the fighter who lost. It does not mean the judges were wrong: stats can’t see damage, power or octagon control. That’s why every row also shows how the media scored the fight, and why some rows carry a limited corroboration flag (fights before 2008, when stats were coded from video years later, or fights with fewer than 3 media scores).

Tiers

Show code 
tb |> mutate(tier = factor(tier, names(tier_cols))) |> arrange(tier) |>
  left_join(mt |> select(tier, media_majority_loser), by = "tier") |>
  transmute(Tier = tier,
            `Score range` = c("< 0.25", "0.25–0.50", "0.50–0.75", "≥ 0.75")[as.integer(tier)],
            Decisions = n, Share = share, `Media majority scored it for the loser*` = media_majority_loser) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(Decisions, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(c(Share, `Media majority scored it for the loser*`), decimals = 1) |>
  tab_footnote("* Among decisions with at least 5 media scorecards.") |>
  opt_row_striping()
Tier Score range Decisions Share Media majority scored it for the loser*
Clean NA 2,841 70.2% 2.0%
Close / defensible NA 618 15.3% 14.6%
Questionable NA 365 9.0% 33.3%
Robbery NA 225 5.6% 47.4%
* Among decisions with at least 5 media scorecards.

The tiers are the cutoffs fixed before looking at the media data (0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75). Media agreement rises steadily across them, which is what a meaningful scale should do.

Show code 
plot_robbery_distribution(ri)

Search every decision

Click a row to see why the model disagrees. Cards list the declared winner’s total first.

Show code 
tier_badge <- function(t) {
  col <- tier_cols[[t]]
  htmltools::span(class = "tier-pill", style = paste0("background:", col, ";",
                  if (t %in% c("Clean", "Close / defensible")) "color:#1B1F24;" else ""), t)
}
tbl <- ri |>
  arrange(desc(robbery_score)) |>
  transmute(Date = date, Event = event, Winner = winner_name, Loser = loser_name,
            Decision = coalesce(decision_type, "Draw"), Cards = cards_winner_first,
            Score = robbery_score, Tier = as.character(tier), `P(winner)` = p_winner,
            `Media for loser` = if_else(coalesce(media_scored, 0) > 0,
                                        paste0(media_for_loser, "/", media_scored), "–"),
            Flag = if_else(limited_corroboration, "Limited corroboration", ""),
            why = coalesce(why, "Draw: no declared winner."))
reactable(
  tbl, searchable = TRUE, filterable = FALSE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, compact = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 20, showPageSizeOptions = TRUE, pageSizeOptions = c(20, 50, 100),
  defaultSorted = list(Score = "desc"),
  columns = list(
    Date = colDef(format = colFormat(date = TRUE), width = 100),
    Event = colDef(minWidth = 180),
    Cards = colDef(minWidth = 220, style = list(fontSize = "0.8rem")),
    Score = colDef(format = colFormat(digits = 3), width = 80,
                   style = function(v) list(fontWeight = if (!is.na(v) && v >= 0.75) 700 else 400)),
    Tier = colDef(cell = function(v) if (is.na(v)) "Draw" else tier_badge(v), width = 140),
    `P(winner)` = colDef(format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 0), width = 90),
    `Media for loser` = colDef(width = 90, align = "center"),
    Flag = colDef(width = 120, style = list(fontSize = "0.75rem", color = "#6B7280")),
    why = colDef(show = FALSE)
  ),
  details = function(i) htmltools::div(style = "padding: 0.6rem 1rem; font-size: 0.9rem;", tbl$why[i])
)

Top 25

Show code 
top25 <- ri_nd |> arrange(desc(robbery_score)) |> head(25)
top25 |>
  transmute(Rank = row_number(), Date = date, Bout = fight_label(winner_name, loser_name),
            Decision = decision_type, Cards = cards_winner_first, `Robbery Score` = robbery_score,
            `P(loser wins)` = p_loser,
            `Media for loser` = if_else(coalesce(media_scored, 0) > 0, paste0(media_for_loser, " of ", media_scored), "–"),
            `Limited corroboration` = if_else(limited_corroboration, "Yes", "")) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_date(Date, date_style = "yMMMd") |>
  fmt_number(`Robbery Score`, decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_percent(`P(loser wins)`, decimals = 0) |>
  data_color(`Robbery Score`, palette = c("#F2C4CB", "#8E0C22"), domain = c(0.75, 1)) |>
  tab_style(cell_text(size = "small"), cells_body(columns = Cards)) |>
  opt_row_striping()

The top 10, explained

Show code 
top10 <- head(top25, 10)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(top10))) {
  x <- top10[i, ]
  media <- if (coalesce(x$media_scored, 0) > 0)
    sprintf(" Media: %d of %d scorecards had %s winning.", x$media_for_loser, x$media_scored, x$loser_name) else
    " No media scorecards are recorded for this fight."
  flag <- if (x$limited_corroboration) " *Limited corroboration: treat with extra caution.*" else ""
  cat(sprintf("**%d. %s** (%s, %s; %s decision). Robbery Score **%.3f**. %s%s%s\n\n",
              i, fight_label(x$winner_name, x$loser_name), x$event, format(x$date, "%b %d, %Y"),
              tolower(x$decision_type), x$robbery_score, x$why, media, flag))
}

1. Igor Pokrajac def. Fabio Maldonado (UFC on FUEL TV: Korean Zombie vs Poirier, May 15, 2012; unanimous decision). Robbery Score 0.998. Model favored Maldonado in 3 of 3 rounds; Maldonado out-landed Pokrajac 98-36 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); Pokrajac had 1 takedown to 0; Pokrajac had 3:20 more control time. Media: 4 of 5 scorecards had Fabio Maldonado winning.

2. Leonard Garcia def. Nam Phan (The Ultimate Fighter: Team GSP vs Team Koscheck Finale, Dec 04, 2010; split decision). Robbery Score 0.992. Model favored Phan in 3 of 3 rounds; Phan out-landed Garcia 102-64 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); Garcia had 2 takedowns to 0; Phan had 1:45 more control time. Media: 5 of 5 scorecards had Nam Phan winning.

3. Sergio Moraes def. Tim Means (UFC Fight Night: Machida vs. Anders, Feb 03, 2018; split decision). Robbery Score 0.990. Model favored Means in 3 of 3 rounds; Means out-landed Moraes 129-87 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); Means scored 1 knockdown; Means had 1:21 more control time. Media: 13 of 14 scorecards had Tim Means winning.

4. Tom Duquesnoy def. Terrion Ware (UFC Fight Night: Werdum vs. Volkov, Mar 17, 2018; unanimous decision). Robbery Score 0.989. Model favored Ware in 3 of 3 rounds; Ware out-landed Duquesnoy 85-67 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); Ware had 1:22 more control time. Media: 5 of 16 scorecards had Terrion Ware winning.

5. Gian Villante def. Sean O’Connell (UFC Fight Night: Te Huna vs Marquardt, Jun 28, 2014; split decision). Robbery Score 0.987. Model favored O’Connell in 3 of 3 rounds; O’Connell out-landed Villante 109-93 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); O’Connell scored 1 knockdown; O’Connell had 4:04 more control time. Media: 3 of 8 scorecards had Sean O’Connell winning.

6. Wellington Turman def. Sam Alvey (UFC Fight Night: Barboza vs. Chikadze, Aug 28, 2021; split decision). Robbery Score 0.986. Model favored Alvey in 2 of 3 rounds; Turman out-landed Alvey 69-68 in sig. strikes (ahead in 1 of 3); Turman had 2 takedowns to 0; Turman had 1:00 more control time; point deduction: Wellington Turman -2 (rd 3). Media: 3 of 13 scorecards had Sam Alvey winning.

7. Sean Sherk def. Nick Diaz (UFC 59: Reality Check, Apr 15, 2006; unanimous decision). Robbery Score 0.984. Model favored Diaz in 3 of 3 rounds; Diaz out-landed Sherk 57-39 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); Sherk had 2 takedowns to 1; Sherk had 2:20 more control time. Media: 0 of 2 scorecards had Nick Diaz winning. Limited corroboration: treat with extra caution.

8. Phillipe Nover def. Yui Chul Nam (UFC Fight Night: Edgar vs Faber, May 16, 2015; split decision). Robbery Score 0.983. Model favored Nam in 2 of 3 rounds; Nam out-landed Nover 29-12 in sig. strikes (ahead in 2 of 3); Nover had 6 takedowns to 2. Media: 11 of 12 scorecards had Yui Chul Nam winning.

9. Priscila Cachoeira def. Ji Yeon Kim (UFC Fight Night: Makhachev vs. Green, Feb 26, 2022; unanimous decision). Robbery Score 0.983. Model favored Kim in 3 of 3 rounds; Kim out-landed Cachoeira 170-102 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); Cachoeira had 1 takedown to 0. Media: 14 of 15 scorecards had Ji Yeon Kim winning.

10. Drakkar Klose def. King Green (UFC Fight Night: Lee vs. Iaquinta, Dec 15, 2018; unanimous decision). Robbery Score 0.983. Model favored Green in 3 of 3 rounds; Green out-landed Klose 92-58 in sig. strikes (ahead in 3 of 3); Green had 2:46 more control time. Media: 11 of 14 scorecards had King Green winning.

TipReading a high score

A high score with strong media support for the loser (for example 80–100% of media scorecards) is the clearest kind of disagreement. A high score with little media support usually means the people watching saw something the counts don’t record: damage, power, or which strikes actually landed clean. Those cases are listed on the Validation page.

Data: UFCStats (via Greco1899 mirror), MMADecisions, BestFightOdds · Analysis by Rob Kirby

 

A robbery here means strong disagreement between the result and the statistics, never an accusation.
